newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Businessman Eduardo Cojuangco would rather support moves to change the Charter and extend the term of President Ramos rather than support Vice President Joseph Estrada in the 1998 elections. Cojuangco lost to administration candidate Fidel Ramos during the 1998 presidential elections. (INQUIRER)
- Former Armed Forces chief Arturo Enrile on Wednesday asked his critics to give him a chance to prove himself as secretary of the Department of Transportation and Communications. (CHRONICLE)

- The Communist Party of the Philippines and its miliitary arm, the New People's Army, have reportedly opened more guerrilla fronts in southern and central Luzon to gain more bargaining power in its peace negotiations with the government, military authorities said on Wednesday. (TODAY)
- The Philippine Central Bank on Wednesday postponed its maiden Yankee bond issue because of poor market conditions in the U.S. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Socioeconomic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito said on Wednesday first quarter gross national product will be less than 7 percent due to "transitory difficulties in the manufacturing sector in 1996." (BUSINESS DAILY)

- Stockholders of Metrobank ratified on Wednesday a 14 billion-peso increase in the bank's authorised capital stock to 50 billion pesos, making it not only the highest in the banking industry but among all companies listed at the Philippine Stock Exchange. (CHRONICLE/STAR)
